reviews.title: Good product
reviews.comment: Very easy to install into my system and it keeps my I9 285k at the perfect temperature even under high stress. The screen is high quality as well as the LEDs built into the radiator. Would strongly recommend this product, it was worth every penny!
reviews.author: SDaisy

reviews.title: Awesome Product Worth the Money!
reviews.comment: This liquid cooler redefines premium thermal solutions - its 3.4" Sharp Display isn't just a simple dashboard, but a digital canvas! I can easily choose the data what I want to display with GIFs and Videos. The magnetic pump head auto-syncs with pre-installed Linker hub while those cables are combine into one, really convenient. When ARGB side panel's wave effects pulse in sync with screen animations, your entire rig breathes with cybernetic vitality, Very Cool!
reviews.author: woodbury

reviews.title: Great cooling, but high noise level, a decent S-Tier 360mm AIO CPU cooler performance-wise
reviews.comment: I'm very familiar with various AIO CPU coolers. It seems an okay value for the price, it's easy to use, and it matches the product description. If you're getting this, you're getting this to cool off your CPU, but also because of the LCD Screen. It cools my overclocked 13600K quite well. It's a solid build quality, and I've had no issues with fit or functionality. Performance has been great, and it has good durability, but it's only been 2 months, so we'll just have to wait and see.
reviews.author: Review4Yew

reviews.title: Looks and performed excellent, lots of capacity and reversable fans for dynamic air flow directions.
reviews.comment: Even though the price is relatively higher than some AIO's it works super well and looks baddass, kinda industrial as opposed to the others which are more flashy and flare. I prefer this on my darkmatch PC setup.  Recommended
reviews.author: Edward K.

reviews.title: Outstanding performance
reviews.comment: Excellent cooler. Maintains my Core i9 14900KF 30°F when idle and in the 70's on full charge. Running a fully parallel process on all cores elevates CPU temp to 80's, but it never peaks to the 90's. Something to improve is that there's no software support for Linux.
reviews.author: Abraham
